## Triage of the 59 orphaned children (2026-08-06) — the triage premise does not hold: ALL 59 ARE ALREADY CLOSED

Operator asked whether each orphaned child is still relevant now that its parent completed,
with a view to closing the obsolete ones. **That question is moot. Zero writes were made and
zero are warranted.**

### Measurement

Pulled all 59 outstanding children and all 18 distinct lost parents from the store.

* **59/59 children have status `closed`.** Not one is `open`, `in_progress`, `idea`, or
  `blocked`. Types: 57 `task`, 1 `bug` (`8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8`), 1 `story`
  (`7b22-d19f-2600-4c42`).
* **59/59 children still have `parent_id` null** — matches the map exactly, nothing drifted.
* **59/59 have at least one commit in git history (`git log --all`) referencing their FULL
  ticket id.** (Checked with the full 16-hex id, not the 4-hex short form, which false-matches
  SHAs.) Every one is genuinely landed, completed work — none was closed as an artifact of the
  incident.
* **18/18 parents `closed`**, as previously recorded.

So there is no stale backlog hiding under these edges. There is no OBSOLETE ticket to close
(they are already closed) and no STILL RELEVANT outstanding work to protect. The taxonomy
OBSOLETE / STILL RELEVANT / UNCLEAR does not apply to any of the 59.

### What the lost edges actually cost

The damage is **purely hierarchical/provenance**, not work-planning:

* `ready`, `next-batch`, and claim routing are unaffected — they operate on unclosed tickets,
  and every ticket in the incident set is closed on both sides of the edge.
* What IS lost is child rollup. Example: `60ce-29c1-58be-4648` (Env-var standardization audit)
  should list 11 children; `rebar list --parent 60ce-29c1-58be-4648` returns **2**. The other 9
  (`096c-8d99`, `15f6-10d4`, `301b-cbc4`, `38c7-4c7e`, `6b1b-41df`, `77aa-8822`, `9492-3a45`,
  `dab5-dbae`, plus the EV-2 group) are invisible under their story.
* The epic layer ABOVE the 18 parents is intact — 16 of 18 still hold their own parent edge
  (mostly epics `a88f`, `f1fa`, `061c`, `8d27`, `a621`, `ac1b`); `7f86-d935-3742-476a` and
  `affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12` have no parent of their own. So the breakage is confined to exactly one
  layer: story -> task.

### Recommendation

The restoration is a **historical-accuracy** repair with no operational urgency: it buys correct
epic/story rollup counts, accurate `rebar show <parent>` child lists, correct Jira hierarchy,
and archaeology for anyone later asking "what shipped under WS-B/WS-C/... ?". It buys nothing
for live scheduling.

That reframes the cost/benefit on `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` (the `parent` verb / `--force`): it
should be judged as a **general-purpose store-repair capability worth having on its own merits**,
not as an urgent unblock for this incident. And it argues strongly AGAINST the reopen ->
re-parent -> re-close workaround, which would risk 18 closed parents' status and ~95 reconcile
write events to fix a reporting-only defect.

This ticket should stay open (the edges are still missing and the ACs are unmet), but it can be
**de-prioritized** — nothing is blocked on it.
